task.title: Merge intervals
task.prompt: Write merge(intervals) -> list[list[int]] that merges every pair of overlapping or touching intervals and returns the result sorted by start.
task.reward: fraction of the five unit tests that pass, measured by running them

result.stopped_because: a trajectory reached the target reward
reflections: merge([[1,4],[4,5]]) returned [[1, 4], [4, 5]], expected [[1,5]]. 1 of 5 cases fail.

merge([[3,5],[1,2]]) returned [[3, 5], [1, 2]], expected [[1,2],[3,5]]. 2 of 5 cases fail. Every failing case receives its intervals out of order and every passing case receives them sorted, so the approach is assuming an ordering the input does not guarantee. Sort first.

nodes.label: one-pass merge
nodes.action: Sweep the list as given and merge each interval into the previous one.

nodes.label: sort, then sweep
nodes.action: Sort by start first, then merge each interval into the previous one.

nodes.label: scan all, not just last
nodes.action: Compare each interval against every interval already emitted, not only the most recent one.

nodes.label: guard the lower bound
nodes.action: Only merge when the new start also falls at or after the previous start.

nodes.label: merge on touch too
nodes.action: Treat intervals that only touch at an endpoint as overlapping: use <= instead of <.

nodes.label: widen both ends
nodes.action: Sort by start, and when merging take the min of the starts and the max of the ends.
